title: Universal algebraic complexity beyond generic corner cuts
objective: Prove a new structural theorem determining or substantially narrowing the worst-case asymptotic number of monomial initial ideals of finite polynomial algebras, starting with three variables and seeking a mechanism valid in every fixed dimension. Establish the strongest relevant primary baseline first. Success requires a complete uniform proof of sharp growth or a substantial asymptotic advance over that baseline for all colength-n ideals or all n-point configurations, a rigorous further algebraic, geometric or enumeration consequence, reproducible exact certificates and an honestly scoped manuscript. Examples, reformulations, already known corollaries and a plan alone do not complete this goal.
relationship_to_previous_goal: A new research objective. The completed corner-cut counting manuscript and its acceptance records remain separate and unchanged in mathematical content.
aspirational_endpoint: Determine the sharp asymptotic order of G_d(n) for every fixed dimension and explain quantitatively when algebraic dependencies increase the generic corner-cut count.

parameters.g_I: Number of distinct monomial initial ideals of I under global monomial orders.
parameters.G_d_n: Maximum g(I) over all fields K and ideals I in K[x_1,...,x_d] with dim_K(K[x]/I)=n.
parameters.F_d_n: Maximum g(I(P)) over all fields and n distinct K-rational points in d-dimensional affine space.
parameters.distinction: F_d(n) <= G_d(n). Do not transfer a point-ideal result to nonradical ideals without proof.
not_measured: Number of polynomials in one Groebner basis
Runtime of computing a basis without an explicit algorithm and input model

starting_bounds.generic: The existing manuscript proves C_d(n)=Theta_d(n^(d-1)(log n)^(d-1)).
starting_bounds.do_not_assume: G_d(n) has the same asymptotic order as C_d(n).

milestones.deliverable: A theorem-level primary-source comparison identifying the best relevant unrestricted and restricted bounds, exact hypotheses, input models and still viable targets.
A precise lemma about multiplication-compatible residue dependencies or state-polyhedron geometry, with its proof attempt and adversarial controls.
A symbolic realizable family and count proof, or a documented obstruction to the tested construction; finite examples alone are insufficient.
Sharp growth or a substantial advance over the strongest checked asymptotic bound for G_3 or all-point F_3, with explicit scope and a route to general fixed dimension where justified.
A proved algebraic, geometric or enumeration consequence beyond restating the count; any speed claim needs a full algorithmic complexity argument.
Complete proof, precise prior-art assessment, independently checked exact certificates and a separate honest manuscript suitable for the user's later review.

passes: Attempt a uniform dependency-sensitive upper-bound lemma
Attempt an infinite asymptotically stronger lower-bound family
required_controls: Onn--Sturmfels: C_2(7)=8<F_2(7)=10; the generic fan is not a universal refinement.
Grid complements preserve the Groebner fan and cannot amplify the basis count.
Every quotient model must satisfy commutation, cyclicity and the claimed length; arbitrary matroid data are insufficient.
Finite-field and characteristic-zero claims require their own hypotheses and cannot be interchanged.
initial_feasibility_gate.after_passes: Record a viable uniform mechanism, an existing theorem settling the target, or a precise remaining obstruction. An inconclusive report prompts a reasoned redirect and does not complete the theorem goal.
initial_feasibility_gate.search_expansion_rule: Increase n, characteristic or dimension only to test an explicit conjecture or discriminate between stated mechanisms.

acceptance_criteria: A theorem for a broad class, not only isolated configurations or a bounded enumeration.
Sharp asymptotics or a substantial improvement over the strongest relevant primary bound established by the first milestone.
A reusable structural proof explaining the effect of algebraic dependencies.
A rigorously established further consequence with its mathematical and algorithmic scope separated.
Exact reproducible certificates supporting, rather than replacing, a uniform proof.
An honest comparison and manuscript; impact, independent verification and journal acceptance are not presumed.

first_feasibility_results.record: docs/interleaving_research.md, First feasibility pass: two rigorous route obstructions
first_feasibility_results.volume_obstruction: For n=binom(r+d,d), the generic state-moment polytope contains a simplex of volume A^(d-1)(A-dB)/d!, A=n(n-1)/2, B=nr/(d+1). This has order n^(2d); the whole-volume exponent cannot be reduced universally.
first_feasibility_results.lower_family_obstruction: For every three-variable quotient obtained by disjoint nontrivial socle relations in an N-point monomial order ideal, g(I)=O(n^(4/3)), n=length(I). This cannot exceed the existing generic order.

first_feasibility_results.decision: Discard only the full-volume shrinking route and disjoint socle amplification route. Continue the primary-bound audit and investigate interacting multiplication-compatible dependencies.

second_feasibility_results.record: docs/interleaving_research.md, Second feasibility pass: interacting relations and a conditional count

all_socle_relation_spaces.hypotheses: I=J_D+R with D a finite monomial order ideal and R any linear relation space supported on its maximal monomials, in any field.
all_socle_relation_spaces.proof: Parallel downward chains from the maximal antichain are disjoint, so each total socle-coordinate sum is at most N-m <= n. Translating away the fixed standard monomials places the variable moment polytope in [0,n]^d. Apply the established lattice-polytope vertex theorem.
all_socle_relation_spaces.decision: Even arbitrary overlap confined to the socle cannot beat the generic order. Relations with surviving nonconstant multiples are required.

conditional_count.hypothesis: For an integer kappa>=1, every monomial box of volume at least kappa*n has quotient residues spanning the length-n algebra.
conditional_count.lemma: The first M=d^d*kappa*n monomials of every generic positive geometric order span the quotient. Greedy independence recovers its standard basis.
conditional_count.further_consequence: For fixed d and kappa, the minimum cardinality of a universal monomial-order list for this whole class is Theta_d,kappa(n^(d-1)(log n)^(d-1)), with the lower bound supplied by one generic point ideal.
conditional_count.scope: A conditional theorem, not an unrestricted bound or a new runtime theorem.
conditional_count.non_generic_control: The published seven-point F_29 configuration with ten initial staircases satisfies the rectangular condition with kappa=1, despite the generic count eight.

unrestricted_obstructions: For n diagonal points, kappa grows as Theta_d(n^(d-1)) even though g(I)=d for n>=2.

Translated Cartesian axis staircases give radical point ideals with g(I)=1, no identically zero monomial evaluations, and minimum representing-word/rank-completion length Omega_d(n^d). A uniform linear representative-word bound is false even for point ideals.
second_feasibility_results.completion_decision: Keep the full goal active. These supporting results identify the remaining mechanism and do not satisfy the all-ideal or all-point-configuration acceptance criterion.

third_feasibility_results.record: docs/interleaving_research.md, Third feasibility pass: binomial quotients and the boundary of the method

binomial_count.hypotheses: Any colength-n binomial ideal over any field in fixed dimension d>=2; monomial generators and nonradical quotients allowed.
binomial_count.conclusion: g(I)=O_d(n^(d-1)(log(n+1))^((d-1)^2)); in three variables O(n^2 log^4(n+1)).
binomial_count.proof: Known binomial normal forms give a partition residue matroid on the known hyperbolic cross V_n. Its moment polytope is the Minkowski sum of the n class hulls. Apply the published O_d(M^(d-1)) vertex bound with M<=|V_n|=O_d(n log^(d-1)n).
binomial_count.priority: Recorded as a consequence of existing tools; no novelty established.
binomial_count.scope: Not an unrestricted improvement, not a sharpness assertion, and not a new enumeration-runtime theorem.

failure_of_automatic_point_extension.circuit: -24+50*x-35*y+10*z-y^2=0; all five monomials lie in V_4^3, every four are independent.
failure_of_automatic_point_extension.conclusion: Five distinct nonzero residue lines have rank four; selecting class representatives independently fails already for a small radical point ideal.
failure_of_automatic_point_extension.limitation: Refutes the automatic partition-matroid extension, not all possible Minkowski decompositions.

finite_controls.models: K[t]/(t^n) and K[t]/(t^n-1), n=4,5,6,7,9, using actual commuting cyclic multiplication matrices.

third_feasibility_results.decision: Retain this positive comparison with surviving multiples, but do not start a separate binomial framework or paper. Continue toward a uniform mechanism for overlapping multi-term circuits under commuting multiplication.

truncated_partition_point_model.family: Distinct positive samples (t_j^A_1,...,t_j^A_d), with A_1=1 and integer positive exponents.
truncated_partition_point_model.uniform_rank_rule: The monomial residue rank is min(n, number of distinct A-degrees); proof by the positive-root bound for sparse polynomials, via Rolle induction.
truncated_partition_point_model.structure: Rank-n truncation of the degree-class partition matroid; genuine circuits of n+1 distinct classes.
truncated_partition_point_model.finite_control: For n=7, A=(1,6,9), t_j=j over Q, 37 initial staircases versus 36 generic corner cuts; all 86 staircases checked, with independent rational Gaussian checks of every positive witness.
truncated_partition_point_model.priority: A finite test of a mechanism, not a new asymptotic theorem or a claim of novelty.
truncated_partition_point_model.next_gate: Prove a symbolic count or a uniform obstruction for this family before enlarging enumeration.

fourth_feasibility_results.record: docs/interleaving_research.md, Fourth feasibility pass: fixed curves cannot supply the required separation

anisotropic_moment_bound.lemma: For an n-element staircase in an integer box q, 2*mu_i <= n*(q_i-1). The old lattice-polytope vertex estimate applied to any subcollection of coherent moment vertices gives O_d((product_i(n*(q_i-1)/2+1))^((d-1)/(d+1))).
anisotropic_moment_bound.dimension_caveat: Add the integral unit cube; the normal fan refines the old one and the resulting full-dimensional volume has the stated product bound.
anisotropic_moment_bound.priority: An anisotropic reuse of the established Babson--Onn--Thomas/Andrews method, not a new unrestricted vertex theorem.

fixed_curve_upper_bound.hypotheses: Every colength-n ideal over any field containing the primitive pure-power relations supplied by A=(A_1,...,A_d), positive integer A_i. The ideal need not be radical or binomial.
fixed_curve_upper_bound.sector: If i uniquely minimizes w_i/A_i, standard exponents satisfy a_j < min(n,A_i/gcd(A_i,A_j)) for j!=i.
fixed_curve_upper_bound.fixed_A_consequence: g(I)=O_A(n^(d-1)) for all finite quotients of a fixed monomial-curve ring, in every characteristic.
fixed_curve_upper_bound.scope: Does not give a new unrestricted upper bound; when the capped ratios grow to n, the expression returns the old exponent.

sharp_restricted_infinite_family.family: The ideal of any n distinct positive samples (t,t^2,...,t^d), fixed d>=2.
sharp_restricted_infinite_family.lower: For n=(d+1)m+e, m>=16d, independently take r_i in [m,m+floor(m/(8d))], i=1,...,d-1; set r_0=n-sum r_i. Weights w_d=d and w_i=d*(r_0-r_i)+i select exactly the n monomials in the d rays x_i*x_d^k, 0<=k<r_i, x_0=1.
sharp_restricted_infinite_family.realizability: The quadratic toric reductions are strict; selected t-degrees are distinct, hence their evaluation columns are independent on every positive sample set by the proved Rolle argument.
sharp_restricted_infinite_family.lower_bound_cost: At least (floor(m/(8d))+1)^(d-1) distinct staircases for every sufficiently large n, including every remainder.
sharp_restricted_infinite_family.scope: Sharp only within this fixed curve. Its growth is below the existing generic lower bound; it does not improve F_d or G_d.

coarse_class_refinement_control.example: The seven-point A=(1,6,9) model has different initial staircases at weights (131,22,27) and (181,26,45).
coarse_class_refinement_control.path_proof: All changes of ground order on the straight segment occur at 0,1/26,7/38,13/50,1/2,29/34,1. The same classes and a strict cutoff gap persist at all boundaries and all six open intervals.
coarse_class_refinement_control.conclusion: One connected coarse halfspace-deformation class contains different bases. A colored k-set count cannot be directly identified with the number of initial ideals.
coarse_class_refinement_control.caveat: The 34 distinct degree sets among the 37 bases are not asserted to count connected class regions.

finite_controls.scope: Finite exact checks support the uniform proofs; the modular rank checks certify rational minors and do not assert a uniform finite-field lower bound.

fourth_feasibility_results.decision: Stop fixed-A enumeration. Any curve-based lower separation needs A growing with n and must respect the explicit ratio bound. Continue an unrestricted dependency-sensitive upper argument or a different realizable lower mechanism; retain the full goal.

layer_upper_bound.lemma: If all staircases in a subcollection satisfy a_j<D, their moment vertices lie in O(nD) integer layers. Each layer has O(n^(4/3)) vertices by the established two-dimensional lattice bound, giving O(n^(7/3)D).
layer_upper_bound.conditional_algebraic_consequence: If I contains a degree-D polynomial with nonzero x^D,y^D,z^D coefficients, its leading monomial is pure in each maximum-weight sector. Thus g(I)=O(n^(7/3)D); D=O(n^(1/3)) gives O(n^(8/3)) for this class.
layer_upper_bound.failure_of_unrestricted_promotion: Translated Cartesian axis configurations of length n=1+3L have g=1 but no such polynomial of degree D<=L. Pure top coefficients vanish by restriction to each L+1-point axis.
layer_upper_bound.scope: A proved conditional bound, not an unrestricted advance. Mixed leading monomials and forced staircases still require a new mechanism.

fifth_feasibility_results.record: docs/interleaving_research.md, Fifth feasibility pass: how many variables can propagate a relation?

failed_gluing_shortcut.component_ideals: The elimination ideals in K[x,z] and K[y,z] are (x^2,z^m) and (y^2,z^m), both with a unique initial ideal.
failed_gluing_shortcut.global_fan: I has two initial staircases, selected by w_y>w_x or w_x>w_y; exact witnesses are (1,2,1) and (2,1,1).
failed_gluing_shortcut.conclusion: The connecting relation has information absent from the two component fans, so their common refinement is not sufficient.

relative_socle_upper.reference: A finite monomial order ideal D, its complement ideal J_D, and a support S_U maximal in s specified coordinate directions.
relative_socle_upper.hypotheses: R is a linear subspace of span(S_U) stable under all remaining coordinate multiplications in K[x]/J_D. Then I=J_D+R is an actual ideal of length n=|D|-dim R.
relative_socle_upper.coordinate_budget: Disjoint downward chains give sum_{a in S_U}(a_i+1)<=|D| for each specified coordinate. After subtracting the fixed standard part, these moment coordinates are <=n and the others are <=n(n-1)/2.

three_variable_refinement.s=1: O(n^(7/3)) by O(n) integer layers and the planar lattice-vertex bound.

relative_socle_upper.product_extension: Also valid for the explicitly justified product reference J_E+(F(z)), whose order-independent diagram and normal forms preserve the relative support.
relative_socle_upper.scope: A support-based construction theorem, not an assertion for all ideals containing a mixed polynomial; no novelty established.

matching_infinite_family.quotient_model: The three socle rows y^3,xy,x^3 map to 1,z^L,z^(2L) in Q[z]/F_L; the other five reference monomials remain independent. The relation kernel is a z-stable module of dimension 2L.
matching_infinite_family.lower_certificates: For L=4m+e, choose a,c in [m,m+floor(m/8)] and b=L-a-c. With u=b-a,v=b-c, weights (3u+6v+5,6u+3v+4,9) select counts (a,b,c) in the three socle progressions.
matching_infinite_family.realizability: Companion multiplication matrices commute and are cyclic. The characteristic-zero socle matroid is uniform by positive generalized Vandermonde independence.
matching_infinite_family.scope: The bound is sharp in this construction along lengths 6L; it does not improve the unrestricted generic lower bound.

finite_controls.field_scope: Only the characteristic-zero lower count is asserted uniformly. All fields have the claimed quotient length but can have different fans.

fifth_feasibility_results.decision: Stop the two-annihilator enumeration. Within this construction, test a relation module killed by one coordinate and stable under two surviving multiplication actions; its proved O(n^(7/3)) ceiling leaves room for a qualifying lower advance. The full goal and acceptance criteria remain unchanged.

remaining_primary_access_notes.status: The primary NSF bibliographic record and indexed Theorem 8 are readable; direct PDF web retrieval fails and an independent public PDF request timed out. sixth_feasibility_results.record: docs/interleaving_research.md, Sixth feasibility pass: bounded connectors also limit sparse plane deformations

bounded_connector_lemma.hypotheses: Deleting k elements from a matroid leaves p direct-sum blocks; the joint internal element-order arrangement of those blocks has R open regions.
bounded_connector_lemma.bound: At most R*(p+k)!/p! distinct minimum bases under generic linear costs.
bounded_connector_lemma.proof: Insert the connecting elements in fixed order. On each previous-basis branch, the maximum member of a fundamental circuit from each block is fixed by its internal order; at step j there are at most p+j possible removals.
bounded_connector_lemma.distinction: Uses complete internal orders, not only component minimum-basis fans. The previous failed gluing shortcut remains false.
bounded_connector_lemma.priority: An elementary consequence of the standard matroid greedy and circuit-update rule; no novelty established.

hook_first_order_family.compatibility: An S-linear phi:M->B satisfies z*f0=y^(r-1)*f1 and z^(s-1)*f1=y*f2. Equivalently f0 is in span(y,...,y^(r-1),z^(s-1)), f1 in (y,z)B, f2 in span(y^(r-1),z,...,z^(s-1)).
hook_first_order_family.length: Exactly n=2m, with free K[x]/(x^2) basis given by the hook diagram D; proved directly using the syzygies.
hook_first_order_family.reference: J=(x^2,x*M,M^2) is contained in I_phi. Reference domain has 4m+1 elements; the variable support has 3m+1.
hook_first_order_family.count: The variable residue matroid consists of a coloop and two blocks joined by three columns y^r,y*z,z^s. There are at most 6(r+s) internal order hyperplanes. The bounded-connector lemma gives g(I_phi)<=60*(1+H*(H+1)/2)=O(n^2).
hook_first_order_family.scope: Uniform over all compatible tail coefficients and all characteristics. Both surviving multiplication actions may be nonzero. This is below the existing generic n^2(log n)^2 lower order, and gives no unrestricted improvement.
hook_first_order_family.negative_control: Adding a constant to f1 violates both adjacent syzygies and forces x*y^(r-1)=x*z^(s-1)=0; it cannot retain the asserted free basis.

sixth_feasibility_results.dense_candidate_obstruction: The initially proposed equal three-plateau/two-action module fits in a reference box of volume proportional to quotient length. The existing moment-box estimate already bounds it by O(n^2), so it was rejected before enumeration.

finite_controls.scope: All full positive comparison chambers are checked against independent Gaussian and relation-row selection. Commuting multiplication matrices, cyclicity, block support, internal region counts and an incompatible constant-tail control check actual quotient realizability. The full report records exact counts and witnesses.

sixth_feasibility_results.decision: Stop enlarging hooks or changing their coefficients. linear_matroid_interface_lemma.hypotheses: Partition a finite vector configuration into blocks E_i with V_i=span(E_i). Put W_i=V_i intersect sum_{j!=i}V_j, q=sum_i dim(W_i), and let R count joint internal element-order regions under linear costs.
linear_matroid_interface_lemma.count_bound: At most 2^q*R distinct minimum bases under generic weights.
linear_matroid_interface_lemma.proof: In a fixed internal-order region every global greedy basis lies in the union of local greedy bases. Within block i, the columns increasing rank in V_i/W_i are forced globally, and exactly dim(W_i) local basis columns remain optional.
linear_matroid_interface_lemma.important_hypothesis: Intersections use the sum of all other spaces, not merely pairwise intersections. Three distinct lines in a plane disprove the pairwise replacement.
linear_matroid_interface_lemma.constructive_consequence: In three variables, per region refine only comparisons between at most q optional columns. At most 1+binom(q,2)*(binom(q,2)+1)/2 cells are needed, giving a per-instance list of O((q+1)^4*R) positive rational weights that recovers every basis.
linear_matroid_interface_lemma.algorithmic_scope: Uses the specified vector representation, exact rank calculations and rational cell operations. No new general bit-complexity bound or coefficient-independent class-wide list is claimed.
linear_matroid_interface_lemma.priority: Elementary linear algebra and the established matroid greedy criterion; no novelty established.

sparse_growing_corner_first_order_family.tail_classification: Writing A_Y=span(y^i:k<=i<r), A_Z=span(z^j:k<=j<s), W=Soc(K[y,z]/M), all module maps phi:M->K[y,z]/M have independently chosen f0,f1 in A_Y+W; f_i in W for 2<=i<k; f_k,f_(k+1) in A_Z+W. The full parameter dimension is 2m.
sparse_growing_corner_first_order_family.classification_proof: Adjacent plane monomial syzygies first force separated endpoint annihilation. The interior recurrence in degrees below k gives f_i=y^(k-i)*z^(i-1)*H, eliminated by the endpoint condition. Higher nonsocle components lie only on the two arms.
sparse_growing_corner_first_order_family.ideal: I_phi=(x^2,g_i-x*f_i for all minimal generators g_i of M).
sparse_growing_corner_first_order_family.length: Exactly n=2m, free over K[x]/(x^2), by the prior direct flatness argument.
sparse_growing_corner_first_order_family.blocks: After removing fixed columns and loops, two arm blocks have residue spaces in x*A_Y and x*A_Z. The core contains the k+2 generator columns and x*Soc(B).
sparse_growing_corner_first_order_family.interfaces: The interface dimensions are at most 3,3,6: only top-arm identity columns and two endpoint tail projections from each arm enter the core. Total q<=12 independent of k,r,s and characteristic.
sparse_growing_corner_first_order_family.internal_arrangement: At most H=10*(r+s+k+1)=O(m) internal comparison hyperplanes; arm columns form three progressions each and the central columns form two short parallel progressions plus four endpoints.
sparse_growing_corner_first_order_family.count_bound: g(I_phi)<=2^12*(1+H*(H+1)/2)=O(n^2), uniformly over all compatible coefficients and fields.
sparse_growing_corner_first_order_family.further_consequence: For each specified quotient, O(n^2) positive rational weights recover all its initial ideals using the proved optional-column refinement.
sparse_growing_corner_first_order_family.sparse_unbounded_corner_subfamily: For r=s=k^3, length has order k^3, the unavoidable staircase bounding box has volume of order k^6, and the number of corners tends to infinity. The result therefore goes beyond the earlier dense-box obstruction.
sparse_growing_corner_first_order_family.scope: A restricted obstruction below the existing generic n^2(log n)^2 lower order. It is not the qualifying unrestricted advance or a publication novelty claim.

finite_controls.verification_scope: Full tangent-space ranks and displayed free coordinates, actual commuting cyclic quotient matrices, reference-border residues, independent relation-row selection, private and optional column flags, and selected exact positive weights. This is not an exhaustive fan enumeration.
finite_controls.pairwise_intersection_negative_control: Three distinct lines in a plane have all pairwise intersections zero and three minimum bases with one internal-order region; intersections with the sum of the other lines each have dimension one. Verified over all four fields.
finite_controls.optional_recovery: At every selected weight, put the forced private columns first and scan only the optional columns; the result equals the full greedy basis after removing known coloops.

seventh_feasibility_results.decision: Stop enlarging the growing-corner family (SC3). The interface lemma narrows the lower route to unbounded interaction or superlinear internal comparison complexity. The thick-hook family (TH1) has been classified symbolically and its natural interface can grow, but pure power-substitution inflation preserves the fan count. Next test tails mixing those residue classes before further enumeration. Continue the unrestricted upper mechanism and primary-bound audit; the original full goal remains active.

next_symbolic_candidate.all_compatible_tails: f0 in Ann_B(z^b), f1 in (y^a,z^b)*B, f2 in Ann_B(y^a); dimensions R*b, m-a*b, S*a sum to 2m.
next_symbolic_candidate.natural_interface_witness: For f0=y^a+z^(S-b), f1=0, f2=z^b, the a*b top z-arm identity columns also occur as images of positive multiples of z^S. An arm/core partition including them in the core has interface rank at least a*b.
next_symbolic_candidate.negative_control: Free extension under Y=y^a,Z=z^b multiplies quotient length by a*b while preserving the initial-ideal count, by the residue-class decomposition and positive weight rescaling. The displayed witness is such an inflation when a divides R and b divides S.
next_symbolic_candidate.next_gate: Use the full compatible tail class mixing power-substitution residue classes, and derive a symbolic count or obstruction. Unbounded rank in one natural partition is insufficient to claim a large fan or an unavoidable interface.

polynomial_interface_count.hypotheses: The previous three-variable linear-matroid interface setting, with q total interaction dimension and L joint internal-order regions.
polynomial_interface_count.reason: After contracting the private columns, only at most q optional columns remain in a fixed region. Their pair comparisons cut its normalized convex polygon into at most A(q) cells.
polynomial_interface_count.priority: Already implicit in the prior constructive lemma; not represented as an established novel parametric-matroid theorem.

full_mixed_thick_hook_upper.family: The full compatible tail class for M=(y^R,y^a*z^b,z^S), a,b>=1, R>=2a+1,S>=2b+1; n=2m, m=R*b+S*a-a*b.
full_mixed_thick_hook_upper.partition: Two arm blocks and a core of 5*a*b monomials. Remove a*b bottom identity coloops and zero columns. Every remaining column has the stated arm or core support.
full_mixed_thick_hook_upper.interface_bound: The core projects into at most 3*a*b dimensions on either arm, so the three interface dimensions are <=3*a*b,3*a*b,6*a*b and q<=12*a*b.
full_mixed_thick_hook_upper.uniform_count: g(I_phi)=O(min(n^(7/3),n^2*(a*b)^4)), over every field and for every compatible tail choice, including mixed-residue tails.
full_mixed_thick_hook_upper.thresholds: Fixed a*b gives O(n^2). More generally a*b=O(sqrt(log n)) cannot exceed the generic n^2*(log n)^2 order asymptotically. An Omega(n^(2+epsilon)) family needs a*b=Omega(n^(epsilon/4)); reaching the one-annihilator ceiling needs at least a*b=Omega(n^(1/12)).
full_mixed_thick_hook_upper.scope: A restricted parameter-sensitive obstruction, not the qualifying unrestricted advance or a claimed new publication result.

koszul_matching_obstruction.constraint: The residue columns are x*y^2 times F,y*F,z*F,G,y*G,z*G. The coefficient vector (5,7,11,-1,-2,-3) is an exact integer relation, by G*F-F*G=0.
koszul_matching_obstruction.nonzero_minor: The exact report records a 5-by-5 minor of determinant 48 in its specified ordering.
koszul_matching_obstruction.generic_implication: The classical relation holds symbolically and the nonzero specialization minor proves generic rank five over Q. The same zero pattern with independent entries has generic rank six. Thus a support-matching transversal matroid cannot be substituted for these convolution columns.
koszul_matching_obstruction.priority: A classical Koszul relation used as a realizability control; no new syzygy theorem or asymptotic lower claim.

finite_controls.coefficient_rule: Saved positive integer coefficients from fixed-seed Python Random instances, traversing sorted allowed monomials. No genericity is inferred.
finite_controls.scope: Full tangent dimensions, actual commuting cyclic quotient matrices and border residues, arm/core support, interaction dimensions, internal hyperplane budget and exact selected-weight basis comparisons. The full fan is not enumerated.
finite_controls.power_substitution_control: A length-10 thin quotient lifts to a length-40 thick quotient under powers (2,2); selected coherent bases are compared at the rescaled weights in all four characteristics.
finite_controls.untruncated_formula: Three rectangle-domain pairs, F=1+y+z and G=1+2*y+3*z, four characteristics and positive/negative finite cost weights verify rank, deleted columns and the reflected Newton-polytope moment formula. One asymmetric case has rank 15 over Q and 14 over F_2; the field-specific erosion formula predicts both.
finite_controls.koszul_certificate_verified: Six-column perfect support matching; exact integer null vector; actual rational rank five; saved nonzero minor determinant 48.

eighth_feasibility_results.decision: Fixed-thickness mixed tails and power inflation cannot supply the required separation. Untruncated two-polynomial blocks are now described exactly, so stop treating their ranks as unexplained or importing support-matching matroids. The concrete remaining symbolic target is boundary-reduced convolution, with growing thickness and its extra annihilator relations. Derive its rank and basis-count mechanism before larger enumeration. Keep the full unrestricted upper route, strongest-primary audit, original objective and acceptance criteria active.

untruncated_two_polynomial_description.scope: Every field and any number of polynomial variables; two nonzero polynomials and bounded convex lattice-complete multiplier domains. No quotient reduction is permitted.
untruncated_two_polynomial_description.common_factors: Remove the common factor to obtain coprime F_prime,G_prime. Multiplication by the common factor is injective in the polynomial ring and preserves the represented matroid.
untruncated_two_polynomial_description.kernel_domain: K0={h in N^d: h+Newt(G_prime) is contained in P, h+Newt(F_prime) is contained in Q}.
untruncated_two_polynomial_description.kernel_proof: Every relation is uniquely (H*G_prime,-H*F_prime). The Newton-product identity makes its allowed supports equivalent to H lying in the monomial space on K0.
untruncated_two_polynomial_description.coherent_bases: At any generic cost weight, choose the largest tagged term c from the G_prime support in the first input copy and F_prime support in the second. Delete exactly c+(0,K0); every other input column is in the coherent basis.
untruncated_two_polynomial_description.basis_count: At most |supp(F_prime)|+|supp(G_prime)| coherent bases, independent of multiplier-domain size. If K0 is empty there is one all-column basis.
untruncated_two_polynomial_description.projected_basis_polytope: T-S0-|K0|*C, where T is the total input cost-vector sum, S0=sum_{h in K0}(0,h), and C is the tagged Newton polytope of (G_prime,-F_prime) including the two input offsets.
untruncated_two_polynomial_description.constructive_consequence: Rank and the entire coherent-basis family are obtained from the erosion lattice set and the small tagged Newton polytope without minor enumeration.
untruncated_two_polynomial_description.limits: Convex lattice-complete multiplier domains and untruncated products are required. Common-factor multiplication can cease to be injective and Newton products can change after quotient reduction.
untruncated_two_polynomial_description.priority: Derived from the classical principal two-generator syzygy, Newton-product identity and complementary greedy criterion. Novelty has not been established; this is not an unrestricted advance.

factorial_prefix_minor.formula: For a,b>=0,a+b<=L, det[(L-1)!/(a+i-j)!]_{0<=i,j<b}=((L-1)!)^b*product_{j=0}^{b-1}j!/product_{i=0}^{b-1}(a+i)!, with negative-factorial entries zero.
factorial_prefix_minor.proof: Row scaling gives monic falling-factorial polynomials at a,...,a+b-1; their determinant is Vandermonde.
factorial_prefix_minor.field_scope: Nonzero over characteristic zero or characteristic p>L-1. Smaller-characteristic ranks are checked separately.
factorial_prefix_minor.priority: A classical Pascal/Toeplitz determinant argument; no new total-positivity theorem is claimed.

one_variable_boundary_amplification.ideal: I_L=(x^2,z^L-x*A_L(z)) in K[x,z]. The checker adds y to embed it in three variables.
one_variable_boundary_amplification.count: Exactly L+1 global initial ideals over characteristic zero or p>L-1.
one_variable_boundary_amplification.proof: Every merged initial prefix of the identity and convolution progressions with at most L columns is independent by the prefix determinant, so the first L columns form the greedy basis. All allocations are realized.
one_variable_boundary_amplification.untruncated_comparison: The corresponding untruncated column configuration has rank 2L-1 and exactly two positive coherent bases. For L>=3, weights (5,2),(9,2) give the same untruncated basis and different boundary bases.
one_variable_boundary_amplification.scope: An unbounded boundary amplification, not an improvement of the unrestricted asymptotic lower bound or a novelty claim.

sharp_independent_arm_family.count: Exactly (t+1)^2 over characteristic zero or p>t-1.
sharp_independent_arm_family.mechanism: After removing fixed summands, a coloop and loops, the residue matroid is the direct sum of the two one-variable arm configurations. Its interaction dimension is zero.
sharp_independent_arm_family.consequence: The earlier O(n^2) hook bound is sharp along lengths 4t+2, but this remains below the existing generic n^2*(log n)^2 order. Further enlargement of independent arms cannot meet the goal.

finite_controls.scope: Every one-arm internal comparison interval and every product internal cell for two independent arms is checked; this covers their full positive fans in each tested field. Relation rows and Gaussian residue selection are compared, and full commuting cyclic algebra matrices check every realized state. All prefix minors and same-Newton-cell witnesses are saved.
finite_controls.characteristic_policy: The uniform count is asserted only under the stated characteristic hypothesis. Smaller-prime counts are reported exactly without promoting them to the same formula.
